title: South Korea's FSC draft digital asset act would make exchanges liable for hacking and system-failure losses
date_note: Date is the FSC announcement day as reported by Financial News (fnnews), whose page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: national financial regulator; Seoul used as the capital, the article names no city
summary: Financial News reports that South Korea's Financial Services Commission announced a draft Digital Asset Innovation and User Protection Act. Under it, operators would bear no-fault liability in principle for user losses from hacking or system failures, shared only if the user acted with intent or gross negligence or a terms-of-service exception applies. The commission could impose a punitive surcharge if an operator breaches its system-safety duties.
plain: South Korea's financial regulator announced a draft law under which crypto exchanges would, in principle, have to compensate users for losses from hacks or system failures, even without fault.
exec: A draft law announced by the regulator would put hack and system-failure losses on exchange operators in principle, with a punitive surcharge for breaches of system-safety duties.

validation.note: Only Financial News (fnnews) was read; the FSC's own release was not read. The draft is not yet law and the article gives no effective date.
